misconception_detail: All 22 stored misconceptions were removed (18 of them catch-all check:'wrong', four using check:'equals'/'close'). Fourteen of the removed messages stated the correct answer outright (for example bronze[0] 'They are both in grid square 8332'). Replaced with 40 expect-matched misconceptions, two per problem: reversed_pairs / reversed_halves (northing written first, expect = the halves swapped) and, at bronze, lines_above_and_right (square named from its top right corner, expect = each pair plus one), and at silver/gold tenths_dropped (four figure answer where six were asked, expect = the two grid line pairs). No message names a number.
flagged_unverifiable: bronze[3] Thurne = 4016 and the original bronze[7] Shallam Dyke Farm = 4016 were identical. Both sit on Norfolk Broads maps (z15 and z16) so the collision may be genuine, but it cannot be checked without seeing the maps. The stored value for bronze[3] was left untouched; bronze[7] was re-pointed at a feature with an independently derivable square.

All 20 problems are image based (OS map extracts on R2). Every stored grid reference was left exactly as found. Internal consistency was checked instead: all eight bronze answers are 4 digits, all twelve silver and gold answers are 6 digits, every tenths digit is 0 to 9, every line pair is 00 to 99. Nothing was silently altered.

silver[1] asks for 'the water close to Chaigley Hall', which is loosely worded (which water feature, and which point on it). Stored answer 686413 left alone; wording left alone so as not to change what the map is being asked for.
gold[4] asks for 'the education facility nearest to the Burnley Wood label', which depends on judging nearest by eye. Stored answer 846319 left alone.
opener_concept: A multi storey car park drawn as an inline SVG grid: columns numbered along the bottom, rows numbered up the side, one car parked in column 3, row 2. The student counts across (3), counts up (2), then texts it as one number (32). The reveal names that as a grid reference and as 'along the corridor, up the stairs', then says maps number the lines rather than the bays and give two figures per half.
notes: Bank shape preserved: bronze 8, silver 7, gold 5, all single_value, all 20 images byte identical (no MC problems in this lesson, so no guided_skip_reason needed). Added tier_guides, guided.opener, guided.teach for all three tiers, guided_steps on all 20 problems, hints, and the three problem_bank tier descriptions (geography had none). Every walk opens by LOCATING on the map: the first live box reads the grid line touching the left of the feature's square off the bottom edge of the map, never arithmetic. The gold teach walk opens by locating the point where a road crosses a river before any number is read. Completion boundary: bronze walks pre-work the easting read and leave the northing, the join and the check live (3 boxes); six figure walks pre-work the easting line and its tenth and leave the northing line, its tenth, the join and the check live (4 boxes). Every walk closes with a check box that reads back the northing half (or, in the gold teach walk, the easting half) with a done note explaining why a swapped answer fails it. Teach walks use self contained inline SVG (a labelled mini map for bronze, an enlarged square with tenth ticks for silver, the same square with an unlabelled road and river crossing for gold) so no map URL was invented. method_card slimmed to 4 steps, 128 words, one compact example. exam_context, topic_links and worked_examples otherwise preserved.
